A relative interior point of each facet moved inward by t preserves its other strict inequalities for small t. Candidate vertex coordinates solve one of finitely many fixed independent normal systems with affine right-hand side. Feasibility and incidence stabilize for t>0 near zero. Each such vertex limits to an old vertex, so the small-erosion fan refines the old one.

Compatibility along a fan cone extends from its rays and then from the vertices of the anchored-weight polytope. On the linearity subspace small feasible radial changes keep positive width, keep original facets, and introduce no facet normal outside the selected fiber fan.

For a singleton fiber each original facet has one owner. Fixing cap coefficients makes its threshold speed zero. In the supporting cases the body-side derivatives are respectively min(δ,0) and max(δ,0), with one common fraction governing the derivative and section allocation. Proper sections have the outward cut normal −u, and lower-dimensional contact has zero area. Endpoint counting handles d=1.

A positive active cap contains a vertex strictly on its captured side in at least one fiber. A positive-area part of an incident facet is strictly in the cap, and all other covector coefficients are nonnegative. Common erosion therefore makes every branch strictly negative and remains in the radial cone. This excludes a radial positive-objective direction with nonpositive cap covectors and yields the Farkas representation with minus active rows.

The constant and radial divergence fields yield section terms s u·c and t s respectively, including both supporting signs. Every affine fiber translation is two-sided lineality. Dilation annihilates all active homogeneous rows, gives dM>0 and forces some cap multiplier to be positive.
